 Concert Review Usher and Chris Brown deliver a very late, underwhelming concert in Atlanta
 The first of a historic five-night run at Mercedes-Benz Stadium was contentious and confounding. Share Usher Raymond kicked off the first of five nights with Chris Brown at Mercedes-Benz Stadium with The R&B tour featuring hits, dancing and pyrotechnics on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. (Ryan Fleisher for the AJC) By DeAsia Paige Updated Nov 6, 2026 With the R&B Tour, Usher and Chris Brown are on the biggest trek of their respective careers, performing in football stadiums for the first time. 
 The name of the joint outing, which began in Denver in June, has a double meaning — signifying their surnames (Raymond and Brown) and the musical genre they’ve both dominated since they were teens. 
 At their Atlanta show Thursday night, the first of a historic five-night run at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, the tour symbolized something deeper — that these two self-proclaimed kings of R&B may not even like each other.
 Put more plainly, Thursday’s delayed concert, with no opening acts, felt confounding and contentious, distracting from the singers’ immense talent and disappointing fans on the opening night in the city Usher calls home.
